report:
## Conclusion: The claim is false — prolonged use of cloth or surgical masks does not cause dangerous CO₂ buildup.

The evidence strongly refutes the claim that wearing cloth or surgical face masks leads to dangerous carbon dioxide accumulation (hypercapnia). Here is what the research shows:

**WHO statement:** The World Health Organization explicitly states: "The prolonged use of medical masks when properly worn, DOES NOT cause CO₂ intoxication nor oxygen deficiency." They acknowledge masks can be uncomfortable but confirm they do not impair gas exchange. ([WHO Mythbusters](https://www.who.int/emergencies/diseases/novel-coronavirus-2019/advice-for-public/myth-busters))

**Peer-reviewed study on gas exchange:** A study published in the *Annals of the American Thoracic Society* (Samannan et al., 2021) measured oxygen and CO₂ levels in both healthy individuals and patients with severe COPD — a group already at higher risk for CO₂ retention. They found that neither cloth nor surgical masks caused clinically significant changes in oxygen or carbon dioxide levels, even during physical activity. ([Annals ATS](https://academic.oup.com/annalsats/article/18/3/541/8419544))

**PLOS ONE study:** Another peer-reviewed study found that cloth and surgical masks did not impair oxygenation or ventilation at rest or during exercise among adult volunteers. ([PLOS ONE](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0247414))

**Fact-checking consensus:** Multiple fact-checking organizations (USA Today, Full Fact, AFP, AAP) independently confirmed that CO₂ molecules are small enough to pass through mask materials, and that while minor discomfort can occur, dangerous CO₂ buildup does not occur with cloth or surgical masks. ([USA Today](https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/factcheck/2020/05/30/fact-check-wearing-face-mask-not-cause-hypoxia-hypercapnia/5260106002/)) ([Full Fact](https://fullfact.org/health/masks-not-harmful/))

**Why the claim spreads:** Viral videos using gas sensors inside masks mislead by measuring transient CO₂ pockets between the mask and face, which do not reflect blood CO₂ levels. ([Science Feedback](https://science.feedback.org/review/videos-use-gas-sensors-to-misleadingly-claim-that-wearing-a-face-mask-causes-oxygen-deficiency/))

In summary, your skepticism is well-founded. The scientific consensus, backed by peer-reviewed studies and major health authorities, is that cloth and surgical masks do not cause dangerous CO₂ buildup in the general population.
